# Review run, CI-fix Repair

After publication, fixes the branch's own failed checks without merging or rebasing the author's branch or stack. Validates the final fix commit before guarded publication and CI watch. An unchanged Repair gets at most one eligible Check re-run.

```
CI failed on pull request <pull request URL> (branch <branch>). Fix only this branch's own failures:
- <failing check>: <check URL>

Also failing on <base>; don't fix:
- <Inherited failure>: <check URL>

Read the failure logs, find the root cause and fix it. Do not skip, disable or weaken tests or checks. Compare each failure with the branch's diff against <base>; a check this branch added or changed is this branch's to fix, even when intermittent.
Read `.thirdshift-review-input.md` for the Spec and Trusted-account input; do not fetch comments. Do not merge or rebase the author's branch or stack, rewrite history, create a replacement pull request or Self-merge. Do not push or edit the pull request or post comments; thirdshift publishes committed fixes with a captured-head guard. If the pull request is closed, merged, draft or changed, stop. Commit only changed files; with no changes, make no commit, including no empty commit. Do not re-run CI jobs yourself or wait on CI; thirdshift owns CI watch and the Check re-run.
After the final fix commit, run final validation as required by the repository's agent instructions in this Review run's worktree. Also run every extra shell command in this JSON list, in order, in that worktree: []. An empty list still requires the repository's final validation. A failed command must not skip the remaining commands. Keep disposable validation logs inside the worktree, never in `/tmp`, so worktree cleanup can remove them. Do not re-run full test suites with `--debug` or verbose trace flags to isolate a failure; re-run the failing test file or filter instead. Inspect large logs with bounded streaming tools (`tail`, `head`, `grep`) rather than reading entire files into memory. If the repository's agent instructions say a suite is invalid from a worktree, do not run it elsewhere as a substitute: report it as `not run against the branch`, with the reason, and never report it as passing. In the final report that thirdshift posts as the review comment, list each exact command and what ran, what passed, what failed and what could not run, with exit status or the reason it could not run. Check the pull request is still open before additional validation; stop if it is merged or closed.
Return a report of the fixes and complete validation results for the final commit. Do not read private Security reports or include Security finding details.
For source edits, prefer an available structured patch/edit tool that makes the intended context and changed regions explicit (for example, `apply_patch` on Codex). Use the Harness's equivalent when available. Normal language-specific code generation and narrowly justified scripts remain appropriate; scope scripted replacements to the intended region and check the diff for unrelated changes.

You run headless: nobody is watching, and ending your turn ends the session. Run tests and other long commands in the foreground, raising the command's timeout if needed. If a command is moved to the background, wait for that task by its own task id or output file, never by process names or patterns (`pgrep`, `ps | grep`, and the like): other sessions on this machine run the same commands. Never end your turn while a background task you depend on is still running: ending the turn kills it. Before ending your turn, stop every background task you no longer need, by its task id (with the `TaskStop` tool, if you have it): a task still running when your turn ends is taken as work you were waiting on. thirdshift records this session as a Session trace, with Model evidence and any review reports beside it.
```
